chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

The morning nap is ill-omened; it drives away sustenance, yellows the complexion, makes it ugly, and alters it. It is the sleep of every ill-omened thing. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, apportions sustenance between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. Beware of that sleep. The manna and quail descended upon the Children of Israel between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. So whoever slept during that hour, his portion did not descend. And when he awoke, if he did not see his portion, he would need to ask and seek (for it).

key_terms.نَوْمَةُ الْغَدَاةِ: The morning nap (specifically after Fajr prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of sleeping after the Fajr prayer until sunrise in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this hadith linking the spiritual and physical consequences of the morning nap to the divine distribution of sustenance (*rizq*) between Fajr and sunrise. The Imam draws a parallel with the Children of Israel, noting that just as manna and quail descended during these hours, missing this window through sleep results in a lack of provision and necessitates begging. This tradition underscores the significance of early morning devotion and alertness in Shia piety as a means to secure divine blessings.
